finalText:
**Most likely nothing is broken.** React re-renders every child when the parent re-renders. It never compares props first.

To make it compare, wrap the child in `React.memo`. That check is by reference, not by value.

An object, array, or function written inline is a new value every render:

```jsx
<Child config={{ id: 1 }} onSave={() => save()} />
```

Hold those steady with `useMemo` and `useCallback`, or move them out of the component. Plain strings and numbers are already fine.

Two other causes worth a look. `useContext` re-renders on any context change, memo or not. And `children` passed as JSX is a fresh object each time.

React DevTools Profiler can show you which prop changed.
